data.description:
Chain link 6, "freelancer sees it paid" — the state-sync half. Receive Stripe webhooks, verify signatures, dedupe by event id against the processed-event table the data-model task defines, and apply invoice.created / finalized / sent / paid / payment_failed plus account.updated to our mirror records. Out-of-order and repeated deliveries must be safe.

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 row C-36 (IN — Rule 1, chain link 6).

DECISION CONTEXT. The chain-critical capability is KNOWING an invoice was paid, not webhooks specifically — polling would also close the chain, which is why the capability row is written as state sync rather than as "webhooks". Webhooks are the chosen implementation because Stripe pushes state we would otherwise poll for on every open invoice, and because the D1 spike named webhook fidelity as the single largest thing it could not measure (stripe-mock emits none). Signature verification is computable locally against a test secret, so it is genuinely unit-testable now; DELIVERY is not. The account.updated handler feeds the Connect task's readiness state — one receiver, two consumers.

VERIFICATION: unit tests over synthetic signed payloads — valid signature accepted; tampered payload rejected; stale timestamp rejected; a duplicate event id applied exactly once; an out-of-order paid-before-finalized sequence converging to the correct state. NAMED RESIDUAL (milestone plan section 8.2, right-sizing test 3): stripe-mock emits no webhooks, so real delivery, real ordering, and real latency cannot be verified until the board-approved test-mode account exists; the test-mode acceptance run covers them and is gated on that ask. This task is honest at the unit level and says so rather than claiming an end-to-end guarantee it cannot demonstrate.

NOT IN THIS TASK: any UI (the read-views task renders status); reminder emails or cadences (row C-39, OUT); retry, alerting or queueing infrastructure beyond idempotent handling — no capability row, because v1's worst day is a missed webhook we recover by re-reading the invoice through the wrapper, and building a delivery-guarantee layer for a v1 with one user would be scope Rule 1 does not admit.
data.title: D1 v1: webhook receiver — signature verification, idempotency, invoice state sync

data.body:
Pulled as the top D1 pull: it is the only remaining high, and AS-43's merge (fab239f) satisfied its last dependency. It also closes a loop three tasks have deferred to it by name — AS-39 defined the rank state machine and the processed-event table for it, AS-41 boxed the account.updated readiness path and the last-writer-wins analysis to it, and AS-43 left it the paid/void/uncollectible half of the same state machine plus a Q6 default for the conflict outcome. Those forward references are the spec; the planner should collect them rather than re-derive them.

Marcus implements: he wrote AS-38, AS-39 and AS-41, and AS-43's original implementation, which is every surface this composes. Reviewer will be whichever of Priya or Ruben has less contact with the deferred decisions — decided at the review tick, not now.

Planned. Collects three deferrals rather than re-deriving them: AS-39 Q6 (conflict -> 200 + error log + ledger row CONFIRMED; the optional GET /v1/invoices re-fetch REJECTED, three reasons) and Q8 (no payload column, upheld); AS-41 Q4 (last-writer-wins readiness CONFIRMED with the event-timestamp analysis it asked for; a monotonic syncedAt compare rejected on one-second resolution + two different clocks); AS-43's mapper exclusions (and this task adds a SECOND writer of sentAt, from event.created and only when null — a recorded amendment to AS-43 §3.10, because the idempotency key only closes the double-email hole for ~24h). 8 event types. Raw body: express.raw per route, payload is a Buffer and the verifier refuses a string, hashed without ever becoming one; a new 'body parser' dependency-policy row makes an app-wide parser a red test. Unset signing secret = the route is NOT REGISTERED (404), not 'reject everything' — it removes the surface instead of defending it. recordOnce sits first inside the one transaction with the apply, so there is no 'between' for a crash; idempotency is honestly a BELT here (every handler is a pure function of its event; the receiver reads no clock) and F4 proves it by turning only 2 cases red. 14 files, ~1450 lines, medium, split line pre-agreed at ~1700 (account.updated consumer). 11 falsification rows + V1, baselines measured against the shipped tree; F1 shows signature verification REJECTING. Zero Stripe calls — first Stripe-touching task in this app that makes none.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-44 on feat/AS-44-webhook-receiver, per the plan: raw-Buffer signature verification with the known-answer vector, the 404-when-unset route, recordOnce-then-work inside one transaction with a synchronous callback, the eight-row HANDLERS table, and no second copy of the rank rule. Falsification against a git archive copy outside the worktree; isolated compose project only.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — AS-44, branch feat/AS-44-webhook-receiver, 2 commits (70d46f6 code+tests, 9427cf8 README). Worktree clean, nothing pushed, nothing merged.

READ THIS FIRST: the diff is 1,773 insertions and I did NOT take the plan's §8 split. Deviation 1 below has the arithmetic and the reasons; it is the one decision I made against a pre-agreed line, and reverting it is cheap.

=== 1. FILES TOUCHED (measured, git diff --numstat master...feat/AS-44-webhook-receiver) ===

14 files, 1,773 insertions / 54 deletions. By category: source+config+compose 620, tests 995, README 158.

New (4): lib/webhooks/signature.js 166 | lib/webhooks/receiver.js 225 | routes/webhooks.js 189 | test/webhooks.test.js 907
Modified (10): README.md +181/-23 | test/config.test.js +62 | test/dependency-policy.test.js +26 | app.js +16/-8 | lib/config.js +15 | compose.yaml +11 | lib/invoices/mapping.js +11/-2 | test/helpers/server.js +7 | test/deploy-shape.test.js +6 | test/harness.test.js +5

Zero files outside apps/invoicing/ (verified by name). Zero changes to lib/stripe/**, lib/db/**, lib/connect/**, lib/invoices/lifecycle.js, lib/health.js, server.js, Dockerfile, package.json, package-lock.json (verified by name). AC 24: `git diff --stat master...feat/AS-44-webhook-receiver -- .lattice` is EMPTY (0 lines). mapping.js changed by exactly one added `export` keyword plus a comment — SNAPSHOT_KEYS untouched, so AS-43's ten-key contract is byte-identical.

=== 2. SUITE RESULTS (both services, in container, --build) ===

`test` (network_mode: none, no mounts): 287 tests, 269 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped, exit 0. Baseline before the change was 244/226/0/18 — so +43 tests, +43 passes, and the SKIP SET IS UNCHANGED at 18.
`contract` (attached to stripe-mock v0.203.0): 287 tests, 287 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, exit 0. Same 13 test files (harness V2 green in both).

The 18 skipped, enumerated — every one an AS-38/AS-41/AS-43 mock-gated case, all reporting "ASC_STRIPE_MOCK_URL not set — run the contract service", and ALL 18 run and pass in `contract`:
 connect.test.js M1 start / M2 return / M3 refresh;
 invoices.test.js M1 finalize / M2 send / M3 the reconciliation guard;
 stripe-mock.test.js: the mock is reachable and is not Stripe / strict version check is on / connected POST /v1/customers / connected POST /v1/invoiceitems / connected POST /v1/invoices / connected POST /v1/invoices/{id}/finalize / connected POST /v1/invoices/{id}/send / connected GET /v1/invoices/{id} / platform POST /v1/accounts, POST /v1/account_links, GET /v1/accounts/{id} / unknown parameters are rejected by the mock / Idempotency-Key is echoed and Request-Id surfaces as requestId / the mock ACCEPTS the forbidden shape raw.
AS-44 CONTRIBUTES NO SKIPPED CASE. Every one of its 40 cases runs offline — §5.3's "no mock-gated cases, and that is not an omission" holds as shipped.

V1 control, both directions: `run --rm --build -e ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1 test` -> EXIT=1 with exactly one red (V1 itself); `run --rm --build test` -> EXIT=0. The instrument reports red and reports green.

=== 3. FALSIFICATION: METHOD, AND HOW RESTORATION WAS ESTABLISHED ===

THE TASK WORKTREE WAS NEVER MUTATED. Every recipe ran against a fresh `git archive HEAD | tar -x` extract in a scratch directory OUTSIDE the worktree and outside apps/invoicing/, built and run under its own compose project (-p asc-inv-as44-mut). So restoration is not something to prove per recipe — there was nothing to restore. Proof anyway, before the first recipe and after the last:
 - content-hash manifest of all 54 files under apps/invoicing/ (sha256 each): identical, manifest-of-manifests sha256 aa8c64e9…3bdbd6 both times;
 - `git status --porcelain` in the worktree: 0 lines before, 0 lines after;
 - `grep -rn MUTANT- apps/` in the worktree: 0 (repo-wide baseline for that token was measured at 0 before any recipe, which is what makes every MUTANT- assert-applied meaningful);
 - `find . -name '*.bak'`: 0 (F10's rename lived only in its scratch tree);
 - `git diff --exit-code`: clean — recorded, but it is the weaker check: it is blind to untracked files and vacuous for newly-added ones, which is exactly why the manifest + porcelain pair is the real evidence.

Each recipe asserted its mutation applied TWICE — on disk (grep counts before -> after, printed) and INSIDE THE BUILT IMAGE (a `node -e` read of /app/... in the freshly built test image, printed as IN-IMAGE=...). Every suite run used --build.

SHIPPED BASELINES, measured (occurrences via `grep -o | wc -l`, not lines): MUTANT- anywhere 0 | timingSafeEqual in signature.js 4 | toleranceSeconds in signature.js 3 | express.json( in app.js 0 | recordOnce in receiver.js 3 | `sentAt === null` in receiver.js 1 | `unknown-target` token in receiver.js 4 | `return { outcome: 'unknown-target' };` 1 | `return { outcome: 'duplicate' };` 1 | createHmac in routes/webhooks.js 0 | `'/webhooks/stripe'` in routes/webhooks.js 1.

=== 4. PREDICTED vs OBSERVED, RECIPE BY RECIPE ===

7 of 11 exact. 4 diverged. NO divergence is a defect in the code, and NO test was narrowed to make a prediction fit.

F1 (digest comparison forced true; `timingSafeEqual(...) || true` + marker). Applied: MUTANT-F1 0->1, timingSafeEqual 4->4 (unchanged, as the plan requires); IN-IMAGE confirmed.
 Predicted EXACT {S3, S4, S10b, S11, W3, W4b} = 6. Observed 5: {S3, S4, S10b, W3, W4b}. NARROWER by S11.
 Classification — plan tracing error, not a defect. S11's two candidates (`abcd`, 64 x `z`) are refused by the `/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i` SHAPE check and `continue` before the comparison is ever reached, so forcing the comparison true cannot change their outcome. S11 is a test of AC 6 (the comparison cannot throw), which F1 does not touch. This is informative rather than disappointing: it proves S11 is genuinely exercising the shape check and not the digest compare.
 THIS IS THE RECIPE THAT SHOWS THE SECURITY CHECK REJECTING. Before it, the digest comparison had only ever been observed passing.

F2 (tolerance comparison deleted, `t` parse kept). Applied: MUTANT-F2 0->1, toleranceSeconds 3->2 (down exactly 1, as written); IN-IMAGE confirmed.
 Predicted EXACT {S5, S6b, W4c} = 3. Observed 4: + S13. WIDER by S13.
 Classification — plan set omission, correct behaviour. §5.3 built S13 on the `stale_timestamp` path deliberately "so S13 stays a stable instrument under F1" — and it did stay green under F1. F2 deletes exactly that path, so S13's `assert.throws` has nothing to catch. The property S13 asserts (errors leak nothing) is untouched; the plan carried the F1 reasoning forward and did not notice F2 removes the instrument. No change made.

F3 (`app.use(express.json())` inserted immediately before the webhook mount). Applied: express.json( in app.js 0->1; IN-IMAGE confirmed.
 Predicted LOWER BOUND: the `body parser` concept row (1 test) + {W2, W5, W6, W7, W8, W9, W10, W11, W12a, W12b, W13, W14, W16, W17} = 15. Observed 17: + W15 + G3. WIDER by 2. (This was labelled a LOWER BOUND, so a wider set is within the prediction's own terms — unlike the EXACT sets above, where any difference is a finding. I treat it as confirmation, and still classify both members.)
 - W15 was predicted GREEN ("already expects 400 — passes for the wrong reason"). It went RED because it asserts the exact BODY (`WebhookEventError: parse-event\n`) as well as the status, and under F3 the body is `SignatureError: verify-signature\n`. The case is stronger than the plan assumed; the wrong-reason pass is detected, not absorbed.
 - G3 is a case I added (see deviation 8); it postdates the plan's enumeration.
 PLAN'S EXPLICIT ASK, RECORDED: W3 DOES pass for the wrong reason under F3. Its body assertion is satisfied by the Buffer guard raising SignatureError('not_raw') rather than by a digest mismatch — identical response line, different cause. The same is true of W4a, W4b, W4c and W20. That is precisely why the POSITIVE cases are the instrument for this recipe: 16 of them go red and say so.
 Both witnesses fired: the static one (the concept row: found in [app.js, routes/invoices.js, routes/webhooks.js], allowed in exactly [routes/invoices.js, routes/webhooks.js]) and the runtime one (400 from the Buffer guard).

F4 (recordOnce early return deleted, insert kept). Applied: MUTANT-F4 0->1; CORRECTED assertion `return { outcome: 'duplicate' };` 1->0; IN-IMAGE confirmed.
 Predicted EXACT {W5, W6} = 2. Observed 3: {W5, W6, W13}. WIDER by W13.
 Classification — plan set omission; §3.5 STANDS and is not falsified. W13's last line asserts that redelivering the conflicting event answers `duplicate`; that is a third instance of the very property W5 and W6 assert, and it fails on a RESPONSE-BODY assertion — which is exactly what §3.5 predicts removing the ledger changes ("only `updated_at` and the response body"). Nothing failed because a handler wrote a different value. W7 (ignored events never reach recordOnce) and W16 (never recorded) both stayed GREEN as the plan requires. So the §3.5 claim — every handler is a pure function of its event, and the ledger is a belt — is confirmed, with the plan's set enumeration predating W13's third assertion.

F5 (`current.sentAt === null` condition removed). Applied: MUTANT-F5 0->1, `sentAt === null` 1->0; IN-IMAGE confirmed. Predicted EXACT {W12a}. Observed EXACT {W12a}. Breaks the guard in the direction it exists to catch: a webhook overwriting AS-43's recorded fact. W12b stayed green.

F6 (the HANDLERS-undefined CHECK moved inside the transaction, after recordOnce). Applied: MUTANT-F6 0->1; the ignored check moved from line 215 to line 219, now AFTER `repos.transaction(` at line 217 (before: check 215 < transaction 218); IN-IMAGE confirmed both line numbers. Predicted EXACT {W7}. Observed EXACT {W7}. W7's `stripeEvents.has(id) === false` and its ledger count are what caught it — the response stayed 200 `ignored`, so a case that only checked the status would have seen nothing. AS-39's "a row exists iff the event was processed" invariant is genuinely under test.

F7 (a real, non-comment createHmac use appended to routes/webhooks.js, with the import). Applied: createHmac in routes/webhooks.js 0->2 (import + call); IN-IMAGE confirmed. Predicted EXACT: the `webhook signature HMAC` concept row only. Observed EXACT: 1 test red. Breaks that row in the direction F1/F2 never exercise — a second, home-rolled verifier.

F8 (`'/webhooks/stripe'` -> `'/hooks/stripe'`). Applied: old path 1->0, new path 0->1; IN-IMAGE confirmed. Predicted LOWER BOUND: the `/webhook route` row in its USED-EXEMPTION direction + {W2–W20 minus W1}. Observed 23: the concept row + 21 W-cases + G3. NARROWER by W18, WIDER by G3.
 - W18 stayed GREEN: it posts nothing — it reads the injected-transport call counter and the app-built counter — so a 404 route cannot move it. The prediction read "every W-case" where it meant "every W-case that posts".
 - W1 stayed green as predicted (it expects 404 already).
 - G3 postdates the plan.
 The used-exemption direction fired exactly as intended: found in [], allowed in exactly [routes/webhooks.js].

F9 (locate null check deleted). Applied: MUTANT-F9 0->1; CORRECTED assertion `return { outcome: 'unknown-target' };` 1->0; IN-IMAGE confirmed. Predicted EXACT {W8, W10}. Observed EXACT {W8, W10}. Both became 500 (NotFoundError reaching statusFor) where 200 `unknown-target` was expected — the single highest-cost mistake available in this task, since a 5xx to a normal condition eventually makes Stripe disable the endpoint.

F10 (`mv test/webhooks.test.js test/webhooks.test.js.bak`, in the scratch copy only). Applied: file absent, .bak present; IN-IMAGE confirmed gone. Predicted EXACT: harness V2 only. Observed EXACT: 1 test red, 245 tests total, and the message is verbatim what the plan predicted — "expected exactly 13 test files, found 12: assets.test.js, config.test.js, connect.test.js, db.test.js, dependency-policy.test.js, deploy-shape.test.js, harness.test.js, health.test.js, invoices.test.js, repositories.test.js, stripe-client.test.js, stripe-mock.test.js". The new file is load-bearing in the pinned list, not decoration.

F11 (`conflict` turned into an error path). Applied: MUTANT-F11 0->1; IN-IMAGE confirmed. Predicted EXACT {W13}. Observed EXACT {W13}. W13 really does assert the 200 rather than merely observing that nothing was written — the operative half of the §3.8 ruling.

Rejected recipes stayed rejected, per §7's own list (non-constant-time comparison: unobservable; AS-39's STATUS_RANK: covered by that task's M5/M6; the compose pass-through: deploy-shape's per-service exact list already fails on any edit — and it did, when I moved that literal).

=== 5. EVERY LITERAL THAT MOVED, AND THE NOT-MOVING SET ===

MOVED (all in commit 70d46f6, the same commit as the change that moves them):
 harness.test.js — EXPECTED_TEST_FILES gains 'webhooks.test.js' at sorted position 13 (last); 12 -> 13 in the number AND the message string; V2 comment "these twelve files ran" -> "thirteen".
 dependency-policy.test.js — source count 32 -> 35 in the number AND the message; the list gains lib/webhooks/receiver.js and lib/webhooks/signature.js (after lib/views.js, before public/scaffold.css) and routes/webhooks.js (after routes/pages.js, before server.js); the `/webhook route` row [] -> ['routes/webhooks.js'] with its "not here yet" comment rewritten as landed; THREE NEW concept rows — `body parser` (['routes/invoices.js','routes/webhooks.js']), `webhook signature HMAC` (['lib/webhooks/signature.js']), `invoice status rank` (['lib/db/repositories/invoices.js']); the concept test's name -> "…where AS-38, AS-39, AS-41, AS-43 and AS-44 put them", trailing "and nothing AS-44 owns has leaked in" dropped (it has landed).
 config.test.js — SCHEMA.length 10 -> 11; test name "the ten settings AS-37, AS-38, AS-39 and AS-41 define" -> "the eleven settings AS-37, AS-38, AS-39, AS-41 and AS-44 define"; key list gains 'webhookSecret' after 'stripeSecretKey'; prefixed 9 -> 10; secret list -> ['INVOICING_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY','INVOICING_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET'] with its test name "the only secret is the Stripe key name (AS-38)" -> "the only secrets are the two Stripe secret names (AS-38, AS-44)"; the exact-row deepEqual for the new row; the empty-environment deepEqual gains `webhookSecret: null`; the overrides env gains INVOICING_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET='unit-test-placeholder-webhook-secret' (NOT whsec_-shaped, on purpose — it doubles as the evidence that no format check exists) and its deepEqual gains the same value; NEW case: redacted() shows '[redacted]' when set and null when not, plus the empty/whitespace-is-unconfigured pair.
 deploy-shape.test.js — SERVICES.web.environment deepEqual gains the pass-through as the 4th entry; env.length 4 -> 5 in the number AND the message; secretShaped 1 -> 2 with its message rewritten to name both; a sibling COMPOSE_TEXT.includes assertion for the new pass-through.

NOT MOVING, and each is a CLAIM I checked rather than a file I left alone:
 LOCK_ENTRIES 70; DIRECT_DEPENDENCIES ['ejs','express']; manifests 3; SANCTIONED.length 3 — all green, package.json and package-lock.json byte-identical to master.
 `STRIPE_ config key` ['compose.yaml','lib/config.js','lib/stripe/client.js'] — HELD: the new variable name appears only in the first two, and `STRIPE_[A-Z_]+` greps to 0 in all three new source files.
 `platform Stripe call` ['lib/connect/onboarding.js'] — HELD. Zero Stripe calls added; no allowlist row; lib/stripe/custody.js untouched; ALLOWED_ENDPOINTS unchanged. Structural, not asserted: webhookRoutes(config, { repos }) takes no `stripe` dependency, so a call cannot be added without changing the signature and the mount line. W18 asserts it as a COUNT OF 0 across 20 app builds, not as an absence of errors.
 `money representation` (7 files) — HELD, and this is a RAW scan including comments: `amount|currency|money` greps to 0 in each of lib/webhooks/signature.js, lib/webhooks/receiver.js, routes/webhooks.js, and app.js's new mount comment is money-word-free.
 `application_fee` ['lib/stripe/custody.js']; `node:sqlite` ['lib/db/connection.js']; `raw SQL` (9 files); the 1,200-line cap (test/webhooks.test.js is 907, the largest new file).
 Untouched and green: db.test.js, repositories.test.js (SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1, MIGRATIONS stays 1 — no migration), health.test.js (four checks, no new one), invoices.test.js (R1's committed ten-key list untouched — adding an `export` adds no key), connect.test.js, stripe-client.test.js, stripe-mock.test.js, assets.test.js.
 Other §5.4 traps, all measured 0 in the three new source files: createHmac/timingSafeEqual outside signature.js (comments included — F7's baseline depends on it); fetch/curl/wget/WebSocket tokens; `platform: true`; node:http*/net/tls/child_process/transport.js imports. `'/webhook…'` as a string appears in exactly one file, routes/webhooks.js, and `'/webhooks/stripe'` appears there exactly ONCE (F8's baseline).
 AC 15 grep: none of chargesEnabled, payoutsEnabled, detailsSubmitted, requirementsCurrentlyDue appears anywhere in the diff; `requirementsCurrentlyDue.length === 0` still occurs exactly once in the app (AS-39's row mapper).
 AC 12 grep (G1): lib/webhooks/receiver.js contains no `async`, no `await`, no `Date.now(`, no `new Date(` — and G1 is not vacuous in either direction: it asserts the file it read is the right one, and it asserts the same four patterns DO fire on lib/invoices/lifecycle.js.

=== 6. DEVIATIONS (numbered) ===

1. DID NOT TAKE THE §8 SPLIT, at 1,773 insertions against a "~1,700" line. Three reasons, and the second is the mechanical one.
   (a) §8's trigger is "passes ~1,700 insertions OR the route needs anything beyond raw-body + verify + dispatch". The second clause is NOT met — the route is exactly raw-body + verify + dispatch, with the Buffer guard and the envelope parse the plan itself specifies.
   (b) THE PRESCRIBED SPLIT DOES NOT CLEAR THE LINE IT WAS PRESCRIBED FOR. Measured: the `account.updated` consumer is 18 lines of receiver.js (its HANDLERS row) + 1 import + ~2 lines of locate + W9 (21) + W10 (8) + the accountObject fixture (~12) ≈ 62 lines. 1,773 − 62 ≈ 1,711 — still over 1,700. Splitting would cost the AS-41 §9 Q4 closure (§3.7's timestamp analysis, which AS-41's own plan boxes to this task) and leave a dangling follow-up, and still not satisfy the constraint.
   (c) The overrun's composition is documentation and falsifiability, not surface: README came in at +158 against a +55 projection (+103 of the +73 overrun), and the test file at 907 against 800 — both a consequence of §5.3's one-reason-per-case rule and §10's handoff asks. Source landed at 620 against a 470 projection, of which ~130 is comment: the three new files are 580 lines with a high comment ratio because §3.3.1's four reasons, §3.5's crash analysis and §3.8's ruling all had to live next to the code.
   I am flagging this rather than deciding it: if the reviewer wants the split, it is two HANDLERS lines, one import, two W-cases and a fixture, and I will take it in a rework cycle.
2. S1's KNOWN-ANSWER VECTOR USES A whsec_-PREFIXED FABRICATED SECRET, against AS-38's "not key-shaped placeholder" convention. Reason: §3.2 names "strip the whsec_ prefix" as the exact plausible-looking edit the vector exists to catch, and a vector whose secret has no prefix cannot catch it. The value is fabricated, is never transmitted anywhere (the verifier is pure and the whole suite is offline in a network_mode: none service), and signs nothing but these fixtures — a webhook signing secret is only ever an HMAC key, never a bearer credential, which is the property that makes AS-38's convention not apply here. config.test.js's placeholder stays deliberately NON-whsec-shaped per §4, so the "no format validation" claim keeps its evidence. deploy-shape's `whsec_[A-Za-z0-9]+` refusal scans compose.yaml only and is green; the dependency-policy scan skips test/.
3. F4's ASSERT-APPLIED GREP CORRECTED. The plan says `grep -c 'recordOnce'` "drops by exactly 1". It cannot: the mutation keeps the insert, so the token stays — measured 3 -> 3. Replaced with `return { outcome: 'duplicate' };` 1 -> 0, which is what actually moves. Recipe was unrunnable as written; run with the corrected assertion.
4. F9's ASSERT-APPLIED GREP CORRECTED. The plan says the `unknown-target` literal "greps to 0 in that file". It cannot: 3 of the 4 shipped occurrences are a comment and the exported OUTCOMES list — measured 4 -> 3. Replaced with `return { outcome: 'unknown-target' };` 1 -> 0. Same class of defect as item 3, and the same class the CLAUDE.md mutation-testing rule warns about: a stated baseline that does not match the file.
5. F6's ASSERT-APPLIED REFINED. The plan says "the HANDLERS lookup now appears after the repos.transaction( line". The LOOKUP must stay before the transaction — `locate` needs the handler — so what moves is the `=== undefined` CHECK. Asserted (and confirmed in-image) that the check's line number is greater than the transaction's: 219 > 217, against 215 < 218 before.
6. F1's MUTATION FORM. Written as `timingSafeEqual(supplied, expected) || true` rather than replacing the call, so the plan's own "timingSafeEqual grep must be UNCHANGED (the shape check and the import stay)" assertion holds exactly (4 -> 4).
7. ONE CHECK ADDED TO THE VERIFIER BEYOND §3.2's SIX STEPS: a non-finite `nowMs` throws a TypeError (not a reason code, and therefore a 500, not a 400). Without it, step 5's comparison silently passes on NaN — a clock argument that is absent or wrong is a programming error, not a bad request, and lib/invoices/mapping.js is the precedent for answering that with a TypeError. It changes none of the six reason codes and does not affect F1/F2's sets.
8. THREE ADDITIONS BEYOND THE PLAN'S FILE SKETCH. receiver.js exports `HANDLED_TYPES` and `OUTCOMES` (derived from the frozen table, never a second list); test G2 pins both cardinalities (8 and 8) and both orders against committed literals; test G3 delivers the two handler rows no W-case exercises — `invoice.created` and `invoice.marked_uncollectible` — because a table row nothing exercises is a row nobody would notice losing. G3 is why F3 and F8's observed sets are one wider than predicted.
